problem:
In **ascending order**, rounded to two decimal places in radians, the solutions to the equation $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ for $-\pi \le x<\pi ,$ are

${x}_{1}≈$
{{field-1}}$,\,{x}_{2}≈$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
We divide both sides of the equation by $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ 2\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =5 \\ 2\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =5 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{5}{2})≈1.190\,29\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places. 

To find another solution in the interval $[-\pi ,\pi )$, we subtract $\pi :$

$$
x≈1.190\,29-\pi ≈-1.951\,30
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places. 

So, in ascending order, rounded to two decimal places, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1}≈-1.95,\,{x}_{2}≈1.19.
$$
